behavior: Usually forages alone, standing motionless or walking slowly through shallow water before lunging at prey. It specializes in crabs and crayfish, often breaking larger prey apart with its stout bill, and may feed by day, at dusk, or at night.
field_marks: Stocky, compact heron with a thick neck and blocky head
Slate-gray body with broad, rounded wings and a short tail
Black head with a broad white cheek patch
Creamy-yellow crown and long pale head plumes
Thick, stout, entirely dark bill and red eyes
Orange-yellow legs; feet project beyond the short tail in flight
habitat: Shallow coastal and inland wetlands, including tidal marshes, mangroves, lagoons, swamps, ponds, rivers, creeks, drainage channels, and damp fields or lawns, usually where trees or dense cover occur nearby.
